P.strength: Boston Dynamics Atlas co-op at the top of the page
P.weakness: C++ depth is thin and buried (one-line EKF bullet, skills at the bottom), with CATIA, thermal and hobby padding and nothing on planning

Q.strength: Deep C++/Eigen EKF work with tests and long-tail debugging (tilt observability, foot slip, contact latency), plus a validated impact-severity metric
Q.weakness: No explicit search, sampling or trajectory-optimization work; dense text is slow to skim

R.strength: Clean labeled bullets, clear about what was simulated, 'optimization' and QP keywords
R.weakness: C++ robotics projects sit below unrelated ML and lab roles; some keyword padding (quaternions, 'optimized' used twice) and no planning work

notes: None of the three shows motion planning, so the decision came down to how quickly and credibly C++ rigor and analysis/long-tail debugging came through: Q puts C++ first, puts the robotics work ahead of side roles, and has the most specific debugging and verification evidence. P buries C++ and pads with irrelevant CAD, data and hobby content.
